name: Republic of the Congo
system_note: A dominant executive in place since 1997.
snapshot: Denis Sassou Nguesso, in power for most of the past four decades, won another term in 2026 in an election held with the internet switched off.
culture: Brazzaville sits across the Congo River from Kinshasa, the world's closest pair of capitals, and the two cities share rumba, Lingala and the dandy culture of the sapeurs. The Poto-Poto school of painting, founded in 1951, gave the country an influential modern art tradition. French is official, with Lingala and Kituba as national languages.
society: Oil makes up most exports and most state revenue, and the country has gone through repeated debt crises and IMF programmes. Most people live in Brazzaville and the oil city of Pointe-Noire, leaving the vast forest north thinly populated. Civil wars in the 1990s, which brought Sassou back to power in 1997, still shape politics and the security forces.

story: Denis Sassou Nguesso first took power in 1979. He lost it in 1992 in the country's first multiparty election, won it back by force in a 1997 civil war, and has held it since. On 15 March 2026, at 82, he won a fifth consecutive term with 94.82 percent (AP via Africanews).

The election had the familiar features of an outcome settled in advance. The government shut down the internet and SMS messaging nationwide. Before election day, Sassou was the only candidate allowed to campaign across the country, some opposition figures were in prison and others boycotted (African Elections Project). Brazzaville's streets were lined with his portraits, but many polling stations had short or no queues, with residents saying there was no point. A 2015 referendum removed the age and term limits that would have stopped him. Congo is an oil producer whose wealth has not reached most of its 6 million people, and much of its debt is owed to China and oil traders. Sassou is now Africa's third-longest-serving ruler, behind only Equatorial Guinea's Obiang and Cameroon's Biya, part of a club of octogenarians who keep winning.
briefing.power: A presidential republic with a dominant executive. The president is directly elected for five years with no term limit and appoints the prime minister and government; the Congolese Party of Labour dominates parliament.
briefing.holders: President Denis Sassou Nguesso, in power since 1997 and earlier from 1979 to 1992.
